blocks.text: Data security is an important aspect of security practices. Organizations need to ensure that data in their cloud accounts is stored, shared, and transferred securely to the right people and services for the right purpose. It is also crucial to know where the data is located, what type of sensitive data (e.g., credit card numbers, login credentials) exists in your cloud accounts, who has access to it, and how secure the data is to prevent any potential data breach.

DSPM continuously monitors and scans the onboarded cloud accounts for sensitive data and vulnerabilities and generates alerts based on data security policy violations. DSPM supports the onboarding of Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts, Microsoft Azure subscriptions, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) projects.
Onboarding cloud accounts to DSPM provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Gain visibility into all the data stored in the cloud accounts.
Detect misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and potential threats that could lead to data breaches.
Respond to security risks and take necessary action to prevent data breaches.

blocks.text: On the Cloud Accounts page (Data Security > DSPM > Cloud Accounts), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View the total number of cloud accounts monitored by DSPM across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
Manage the cloud accounts:
Monitoring & Autodetection: Add new accounts to the monitoring scope and enable autodetection.
Business Units Mapping: Assign a different business unit to the account.
Manage Regions: Select regions that must be monitored and scanned or configure regions to deploy scanning resources for custom network configuration.
Manage Custom Tags: Add, edit, or delete custom tags.
Manage Notification Emails: Add email addresses of the recipient to be notified of any configuration or permissions issues while onboarding.
Managing Orchestrator Network (Custom): Configure the orchestrator network (applicable only if the DSPM Connection Status is failed). To learn more, see Viewing Orchestrator Status.
On Demand Validation: Validate the onboarded accounts.
Configure New Orchestrator (Zscaler): Change the orchestrator account.
Delete Account: Delete or offboard an account.
The following features are specific to cloud service providers:
AWS: Manage CloudTrail, Manage Services, Manage Evidence, and Manage Data Events.
Azure: Change Application Details, Manage Private Endpoint, Manage Services, and Manage Evidence.
GCP: Update Service Account and Update Private Key.
Onboard an AWS organization, GCP organization, or a Microsoft Azure tenant.

When the onboarding process is completed successfully, you can view the following tabs:
Overview: The onboarding status and the orchestrator details.
Subscriptions, Projects, or Accounts (based on the cloud account): Details of the onboarded cloud account.
Issues: The issues encountered while onboarding.
Roles and Templates: The roles created while onboarding and templates generated by DSPM.
